title: Read each capability's readiness, KNOWN to VERIFIED, from the facts GREG already keeps, and report where its readers disagree
problem: Directive section 32 asks GREG to distinguish KNOWN, INSTALLED, CREDENTIALLED, GRANTED, EXERCISED and VERIFIED for every capability, and not to count raw tools as success. Section 70 asks after every session what real GREG can now reliably do. At b1950be2 (#196 head) no reader separated those rungs: `greg readiness` was an argparse 'invalid choice', and the unit's 26 tests fail there (21 on `cannot import name 'readiness'`, 5 on the missing subcommand). The readers that did exist answered different questions and disagreed without saying so: Mission Control's classify_capability marks every capability that declares a credential BLOCKED 'needs credentials' even when the secret store holds every declared handle; body.status, and so Mission Control's capability list, holds only built-ins and omits capabilities Genesis registered; routing.track_record reads completed actions only, so a capability verified only as a closure's sensor has no verified count there, and it credits every completed action of a verified mission, including one whose receipt routing itself ruled ineffective.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (directive sections 32 CAPABILITY BROKER, 26 INSTALLABLE PRODUCT EXPERIENCE and 70 REQUIRED QUESTION; recorded on #227)
INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN (build the whole directive first; the founder-device run comes after, as its acceptance; recorded on #227)
INTENT-2026-09-25-SPIDER-WEB-COMPOUNDING (optimize for verified outcomes, not the number of tools; greg/routing.py is its enforcement)
baseline: b1950be2: greg.capabilities.BUILTINS declares 163 manifests; CapabilityManifest.available() checks platforms and binaries; SecretBroker.names() lists handle names; MissionBook holds founder-signed missions and their cones; greg.missions.pre_approved decides signed pre-approvals; Gate receipts record each act; the separate appraiser records mission.appraised verdicts; routing.track_record and routing.reliability score capabilities from completed actions; mission_control.classify_capability gives Mission Control's class; body.status lists the built-in inventory. `greg routing` prints routing knowledge. Nothing reads these together per capability.

alternatives.name: Proposed: a read-only ladder over the existing readers, printed by `greg readiness`
alternatives.description: New greg/readiness.py and one subcommand in greg/cli.py. For every capability in the registry the body uses (the 163 built-ins and every capability Genesis registered on the journal, as Genesis.restore re-registers them), each rung is read from the reader that already computes it: KNOWN from BUILTINS or capability.registered events of a formed provider; INSTALLED from CapabilityManifest.available() and, for an installed:python: provider, the pinned distribution version through importlib.metadata (nothing imported); CREDENTIALLED from SecretBroker.names() only, never a value; GRANTED from an ACTIVE, unpaused MissionBook mission whose signed cone admits the capability (pattern, ceiling, targets, horizon), or a signed pre-approval that greg.missions.pre_approved admits for the step's own strategy, with the capability ATTACHED; EXERCISED from a positive Gate receipt whose witness names it; VERIFIED from a VERIFIED mission.appraised of a closure that judged one of its receipts, with no later REFUTED appraisal or ineffective routing.outcome, and never crediting a receipt the body blamed. Each row carries Mission Control's class and routing's track record, names its first missing rung and why, and the readout lists where readers disagree.
advantages: One per-capability answer to section 32's six rungs, each with evidence references and the first missing rung's reason
Reuses existing readers only: manifests, SecretBroker names, MissionBook, missions.pre_approved, Gate receipts, the separate appraiser's verdicts, routing verdicts; no new store and no new authority
Reports four kinds of disagreement between existing readers instead of smoothing them over
Writes nothing and never resolves a secret value: hash probes of two bodies before and after showed no change, and a planted secret value never reaches the output
disadvantages: Mission Control does not show the counts: greg/mission_control.py is edited by open draft PR #178 (head e410977d), and the unit's scope allows the change only when no open PR edits it
GRANTED does not read the body-wide PAUSE or STOP, the cone's remaining budget, its data classes or the constitution's policy, so it can read reached where a step would still wait

Couples to the shapes of many records (receipts, mission.action, mission.appraised, routing.outcome, capability.registered and capability.state) and to two names in greg/mission_control.py (_providers, classify_capability)

Covers section 32's six-rung distinction, not its full capability contract (permissions, network and filesystem access, data classes, budget, health, provenance, attach, detach, rollback and authority ceiling are not printed)
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained as proposed; revisit when Mission Control can carry it (#178 no longer edits greg/mission_control.py) or when a founder-body readout shows a rung misread.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: derive the rungs from the existing inventory and track record
alternatives.description: Take KNOWN and INSTALLED from body.status, EXERCISED from track_record's done count and VERIFIED from its verified count; add one column to `greg status` or `greg routing`. No new module.
advantages: A few lines over two readers that already exist and are already printed
disadvantages: body.status lists only built-ins, so capabilities Genesis registered would be missing (shown in the unit's tests)
track_record counts no verified action for a capability verified only as a closure's sensor: foundry.query and institution.appraise on the rehearsal body would read not verified

track_record credits every completed action of a verified mission, including one whose receipt routing ruled ineffective (review finding F1's class), so a strategy that changed nothing would read VERIFIED
Neither reader knows CREDENTIALLED or GRANTED; Mission Control's class reads BLOCKED for a declared credential even when the store holds the handle
alternatives.revival_evidence: If the founder rules that routing's semantics are the intended ones, the ladder's VERIFIED can be re-pointed at track_record and this alternative becomes the implementation.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: a full section-32 capability contract registry
alternatives.description: Give every capability a persisted contract record with all of section 32's fields (ID, version, provider, function, permissions, inputs, outputs, credentials, targets, network and filesystem access, data classes, budget, consequence class, health, failure state, provenance, tests, limitations, attach, detach, rollback, authority ceiling) and the six rungs, maintained as a materialized view updated from events.
advantages: Covers section 32's whole contract, not only the rungs
Cheap to query once materialized; a natural feed for Mission Control's founder mode (section 26)
disadvantages: A second, written record of capability state that can drift from the journal it is derived from
Needs edits to greg/capabilities.py and greg/missions.py, which six open PRs hold (#178, #201, #209, #214, #228, #229)
Much larger; nothing about it was built or measured here
alternatives.revival_evidence: When the founder's surfaces need the full contract; build it first as a read-only projection like this one, not as a written store.

alternatives.name: Staged, reversible experiment: ship the ladder as a draft child of #196, CLI only
alternatives.description: This branch. The ladder runs only when someone types `greg readiness`; it reads the journal through observe() and writes nothing. Mission Control parity, GRANTED's missing conditions and the reader rulings come later; the founder-device readout is the acceptance under INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN.
advantages: Nothing in the body changes until someone runs the command, and running it changes nothing
One revert removes it; there is no state to migrate
disadvantages: The founder's main surface, Mission Control, does not show it yet
Every result so far is from local test bodies and a rehearsal body with a REHEARSAL key
alternatives.revival_evidence: This is how the proposed design is meant to be adopted; it is the review trigger for the decision below.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: No reader says which capabilities GREG has installed, credentialled, been granted, exercised or had independently verified. Mission Control's credential class, body.status's built-in-only list and track_record's action-only counts keep disagreeing silently, and section 70's question has no instrument except counting tools, which section 32 forbids.
advantages: No new module and no new subcommand
No coupling to the shapes of six kinds of record
disadvantages: The founder cannot see why a capability is unusable (not installed, missing a named credential, no live grant) without reading the journal

roles.position: Section 32 names the six rungs and says not to count raw tools; section 70 asks what real GREG can now reliably do. The ladder makes both executable on the canonical path: per capability, the rungs reached with evidence, and per rung a count, where only VERIFIED is the rung an independent appraiser stands behind. Section 26's founder mode should expose capabilities, permissions and blockers; the first-missing reason ('no stored credential named github_token', 'no open founder-signed mission's light cone admits it') is that blocker.
material_concerns: The unit's own acceptance item 'mission_control shows the same counts' is not met; a carried class and a parity test stand in for it
Rehearsal counts (8 of 163 VERIFIED) are from a REHEARSAL key and must never be read as VEPMC or founder-device evidence

roles.position: One new read-only module and one subcommand. Every rung is read through an existing reader; the module owns no state, adds no store and changes no other module. greg/mission_control.py, greg/routing.py, greg/missions.py, greg/body.py, greg/capabilities.py, greg/appraisal.py and canonical-ci.yml are untouched.

The ladder covers the six rungs, not section 32's full contract fields

pass_1.intended_outcome: For any capability, GREG says which of KNOWN, INSTALLED, CREDENTIALLED, GRANTED, EXERCISED and VERIFIED it has reached, on what evidence, and what its next use needs, crediting success and authority only as the body's own readers do, writing nothing and revealing no secret value.

advantages.statement: One per-capability answer to section 32's six rungs, with evidence references and the first missing rung's reason
advantages.amplified_value: The first-missing reason is the founder's blocker list for section 26 (a named credential, a platform, a live grant); it reverses into a liability if a rung reads reached where the body would still refuse, which is why GRANTED and VERIFIED are decided by the engine's and appraiser's own tests

advantages.statement: Reader disagreements are reported, not smoothed
advantages.amplified_value: Four disagreements between existing readers became visible (Mission Control's credential class, body.status's built-in-only list, track_record's sensor gap and its crediting of ineffective receipts); each is a decision the founder or a maintainer can now make on evidence
Safe to run on a live body at any time; it can feed founder surfaces without a new authority or write path

advantages.statement: Counts per rung, with VERIFIED named as the only appraiser-backed rung
advantages.amplified_value: Section 70's question gets an instrument that cannot be satisfied by adding tools: on the rehearsal body 8 of 163 are VERIFIED, not 163

disadvantages.statement: Mission Control, the founder's main surface, does not show the ladder; the unit's parity acceptance item is incomplete
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Each row carries Mission Control's own class, and a test checks that class equals what classify_capability gives the body.status row; the panel waits until #178 no longer edits greg/mission_control.py

disadvantages.statement: GRANTED does not read the body-wide PAUSE or STOP, the cone's remaining budget, its data classes or constitutional policy
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Every readout carries a 'limits' field that states this; GRANTED through a pre-approval is decided by missions.pre_approved, the engine's own test

disadvantages.statement: VERIFIED is more conservative than routing: any REFUTED of a closure that judged the capability's receipts demotes it, a failure closure's included, and a VERIFIED closure credits no receipt the body blamed
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Where routing differs, the ladder reports a disagreement; the demotion rule follows the scope's binding sentence 'a REFUTED latest outcome never reads VERIFIED', and the reason names a failure closure

disadvantages.statement: CREDENTIALLED reads handle names in the body's file store only
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Stated in the readout's limits: a macOS Keychain item reads missing until a capability resolves it; a store that is a JSON list of strings is read as names, as the broker reads it

disadvantages.statement: The ladder couples to the shapes of six kinds of record and to two names in greg/mission_control.py
disadvantages.redesigned_response: 26 tests and 38 mutants pin each reading; the imported mission_control names exist at the base and at #178's head

disadvantages.statement: Seven kinds of fact the tests judge are recorded directly in their writers' fields
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Listed in the test docstring and the README; every VERIFIED and REFUTED verdict comes from the body's separate appraiser, and F1's test drives the real engine tick

pass_2.final_design: greg/readiness.py: a read-only fold over the registry the body uses (163 built-ins plus formed Genesis registrations), with KNOWN, INSTALLED, CREDENTIALLED (names only), GRANTED (live signed cone or missions.pre_approved, ATTACHED), EXERCISED (positive Gate receipt) and VERIFIED (appraiser VERIFIED of a judging closure, no later REFUTED or ineffective verdict, blamed receipts never credited); each row carries Mission Control's class and routing's track record; disagreements, a per-rung summary and stated limits are printed by `greg readiness [--capability ID]`. 26 tests and 38 mutants.

entries.position: GRANTED should not read reached while the body-wide PAUSE or STOP stands or the cone's budget is spent; until it reads them it should say 'admitted by a live cone', not 'granted'. An unknown --capability id should be reported, not answered with an empty list.
entries.rationale: A rung that reads reached where the body would still refuse overstates readiness, the defect class the review round fixed for VERIFIED and pre-approval
entries.evidence_threshold: A body under PAUSE or STOP, or with a spent cone, whose readout shows GRANTED reached for a step the engine refuses
entries.review_trigger: Before any founder surface (Mission Control) shows GRANTED

entries.position: A REFUTED appraisal of a failure closure can mean the capability worked (the claimed failure could not be verified); demoting VERIFIED for it may hide a success.
entries.rationale: Attack review F3: the appraiser returns REFUTED for an unmet closure when the receipts or a re-observation satisfy the check
entries.evidence_threshold: A founder ruling that failure-closure refutations should not demote, or a real body where such a refutation hid a verified capability
entries.review_trigger: The founder's ruling on VERIFIED semantics
